title: Sampling and estimation
overview: Understand sampling distributions and construct confidence intervals to estimate an unknown population parameter. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Explain why random sampling matters and identify biased procedures.
Use the sampling distribution of the sample mean and the Central Limit Theorem.
Calculate unbiased estimates of population mean and variance.
Construct and interpret confidence intervals for a mean or large-sample proportion.

definitions.definition: The full set about which an inference is made.
A subset observed to learn about the population.
The probability distribution of a statistic over repeated samples.
The standard deviation of a sampling distribution.
A range generated by a method that captures the true parameter at a stated long-run rate.

sections.title: Random samples and bias
content: Every population member should have an appropriate chance of selection. Convenience, voluntary-response and incomplete-frame samples can be biased. Random numbers help choose units without personal judgement.
bullets: A large biased sample is still biased.
Distinguish sampling variation from measurement error.

sections.title: Sample mean distribution
content: If population mean is μ and variance σ², then E(X̄)=μ and Var(X̄)=σ²/n. X̄ is normal if the population is normal and approximately normal for large n by the CLT.
bullets: Increasing n reduces standard error by the square-root law.

sections.title: Unbiased estimates
content: Estimate μ by x̄. Estimate population variance with s²=Σ(x−x̄)²/(n−1), equivalently [Σx²−(Σx)²/n]/(n−1). The n−1 correction makes the estimating process unbiased.
bullets: Use the sample variance requested, not the descriptive variance with denominator n.
Keep x̄ unrounded in the variance formula.

sections.title: Confidence intervals
content: For known σ or a large sample, a confidence interval for μ is x̄±z*σ/√n, replacing σ by s for a large sample when needed. For a large-sample proportion p, use p̂±z*√[p̂(1−p̂)/n]. Interpret the confidence level as a property of the method.
bullets: Give interval endpoints in context and sensible units.

examTips: Name the parameter and confidence level in the interpretation sentence.
Check that a proportion interval stays sensible relative to 0 and 1.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Saying there is a 95% probability a fixed calculated interval contains a fixed parameter.
Using denominator n for the required unbiased sample-variance estimate.

quickRecall.question: What is the standard error of X̄?
Why is n−1 used in the sample variance?
quickRecall.answer: It corrects the systematic underestimation and makes the estimator unbiased.

quickRecall.question: What does a 95% confidence method mean?
quickRecall.answer: Across repeated samples, about 95% of intervals produced by the method contain the true parameter.
